before.title: Lighthouse of Pharos Point - Community Wiki
blocks: # Lighthouse of Pharos Point
The lighthouse stands on a granite headland at the mouth of the estuary. It was first lit in 1852 and automated in 1981, when the last keepers left.
## Early history
The first tower was built of timber and burned down within a decade. The current stone tower replaced it in 1862, using granite quarried on the headland itself.
## The light
The lens is a first-order Fresnel lens made in Paris. It turns on a bath of mercury and shows two white flashes every fifteen seconds, visible for about twenty nautical miles.
## Visiting
The grounds are open to walkers all year. The tower itself can be climbed on summer weekends with a guide from the local heritage society.

blocks: # Lighthouse of Pharos Point
The lighthouse stands on a granite headland at the mouth of the estuary. It was first lit in 1852 and automated in 1981, when the last keepers left.
## History
The first tower was built of timber and burned down within a decade. The current stone tower replaced it in 1862, using granite quarried on the headland itself.
During the great storm of 1903 the keepers kept the light burning for three nights without relief, and a lifeboat crew was guided home by its beam.
## The light
The lens is a first-order Fresnel lens made in Paris. It floats on mercury and still shows two white flashes every fifteen seconds.

blocks: # Pharos Point
Pharos Point is a granite headland on the north shore of the estuary, known for its lighthouse, its seabird colonies and its dangerous tidal race.
## Geology
The headland is the eroded root of an old volcano. Its pink granite was quarried until the 1920s for harbour walls along the coast.
## Wildlife
Guillemots, razorbills and a small colony of puffins nest on the cliffs from April to July. Grey seals haul out on the rocks below.
## Lighthouse
The lighthouse was first lit in 1852 and automated in 1981.
